deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page): 𝒜 is a von Neumann algebra with a fixed faithful normal semifinite trace T. Its definition ideal 𝔞 is the two-sided ideal whose positive part is {A ≥ 0 : T(A) < ∞}. 𝔟 is introduced at the end of the previous page and the top of this one. The internal evidence (the remark 'b = 𝒜 iff 𝔞 = 𝒜', and the next-page argument that a projection E which is a norm limit of elements of 𝔞 lies in 𝔞) shows that 𝔟 is the norm closure of 𝔞. That is the closed two-sided ideal of what are today called τ-compact operators.

Statements on this page:
(1) 𝔟 = 𝒜 if and only if 𝔞 = 𝒜, i.e. if and only if T is a finite trace (T(A) < ∞ for all A ∈ 𝒜⁺). Reason: if 1 is a norm limit of elements of 𝔞, then 𝔞 contains an invertible element, so 1 ∈ 𝔞.
(2) A first, crossed-out Proposition 1: for A in 𝔟, the spectral projections of A (for sets away from 0) lie in 𝔞. If E is such a projection, one must show T(E) < ∞.
(3) A reformulated, also crossed-out, Proposition 1: let A be a normal operator in 𝔟 and f a bounded Borel function on ℂ vanishing in a neighbourhood of 0. Then f(A) ∈ 𝔞.
(4) Sketch of proof. A generates a commutative C*-subalgebra 𝔠 ⊂ 𝔟, identified by Gelfand with C₀(Ω), and A corresponds to a function φ on Ω. Then f(A) is the operator given by the bounded Borel function f∘φ on Ω. This function is supported in the compact set {|φ| ≥ ε}, so it is majorised by a multiple of the characteristic function of a compact set. It is therefore enough to prove a corollary: K(Ω) ⊂ 𝔞, i.e. compactly supported functions in the commutative subalgebra of 𝔟 already lie in 𝔞. That statement becomes Proposition 5 on the next page, proved by the trick 'E = lim C_i with E C_i E = C_i, ‖E − C_i‖ ≤ 1/2 ⇒ E ≤ 2C_i ⇒ E ∈ 𝔞'.

Purpose: this is part of section 4 ('Mesures spectrales et sous-espaces spectraux d'opérateurs') of a draft on traces on von Neumann algebras. It is preparatory to spectral distribution functions and rearrangements of operators relative to a trace, the material of Grothendieck's Séminaire Bourbaki exposé on rearrangements and convexity inequalities in von Neumann algebras with a trace (1955).
errors: 'A à une fonction φ sur C₀(Ω)' should read 'a function φ on Ω'. A is identified with an element of C₀(Ω), i.e. a function on Ω, not a function on C₀(Ω). The same slip occurs for 'f(φ) sur C₀(Ω)'.

The reduction step 'majorised by the characteristic function of a compact set' implicitly needs two facts. First, that the projection χ_{|φ|≥ε}(A) lies in 𝔟. This holds because closed two-sided ideals of a C*-algebra are hereditary and the projection is dominated by g(A) for a continuous g vanishing near 0. Second, that a projection in 𝔟 lies in 𝔞, which is proved only on the next page. The page itself leaves these unproved; it is a draft whose blocks are crossed out.
In 'pour toute famille filtrante croissante majorée' (previous page), the boundedness hypothesis is fine. No genuine mathematical error is visible here; the statements are correct.

ideas.what: The norm closure 𝔟 of the definition ideal of a normal semifinite trace equals the whole algebra iff the trace is finite.
ideas.modern_name: Ideal of τ-compact operators; triviality criterion
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; relative compact ideal studied by Breuer (1968–69), Sonis, Fack–Kosaki (1986)
ideas.where_published: Possibly implicit in Grothendieck, Séminaire Bourbaki exposé 113 (1955) on rearrangements in von Neumann algebras with trace

ideas.what: For a normal operator A in the norm-closed ideal 𝔟, f(A) ∈ 𝔞 for every bounded Borel f vanishing near 0. Equivalently, spectral projections of A away from 0 have finite trace.
ideas.modern_name: Spectral characterization of τ-compact operators (μ_t(A) → 0, equivalently τ(E_{(ε,∞)}(|A|)) < ∞ for all ε > 0)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Breuer (Fredholm theories in von Neumann algebras, 1968–69); Fack–Kosaki (generalized s-numbers, 1986)
ideas.where_published: Possibly in Séminaire Bourbaki exp. 113 (1955), unsure of exact formulation

ideas.what: Reduction via Gelfand C₀(Ω) to showing K(Ω) ⊂ 𝔞 for the commutative C*-subalgebra generated by A (developed on the next page as Proposition 5).
ideas.modern_name: Pedersen-ideal-type argument: the minimal dense ideal contains compactly supported functional calculus
ideas.usually_credited_to: G. K. Pedersen (1966, minimal dense ideal of a C*-algebra)

missed.claim: In 1953 Grothendieck was already working with the norm-closed ideal generated by the trace-finite elements of a semifinite von Neumann algebra (the 'τ-compact' ideal) and its spectral characterization. This predates Breuer's relative compact operators (1968) by about 15 years. It is a priority detail for the history of noncommutative compactness and rearrangement theory, not a new theorem.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical attribution only. Fack–Kosaki-style s-number theory and relative Fredholm theory have roots in Grothendieck's 1953–55 trace work. Whether this specific ideal appears in exposé 113 is unclear to me.

deep.surprise_reason: These are correct but now standard facts about τ-compact operators relative to a normal semifinite trace, written as a heavily crossed-out draft. The only point of interest is the early date (1953) relative to Breuer and Fack–Kosaki. Grothendieck's 1955 Bourbaki exposé already shows he worked in this area, so the novelty is modest.
transcription_corrections: 'Pour que b = A' and 'a = A': A here is the script 𝒜 (the whole von Neumann algebra), i.e. 'Pour que 𝔟 = 𝒜 … que 𝔞 = 𝒜'.
'(i.e. T(A) < ∞ pour A ∈ A⁺)' should read 'pour A ∈ 𝒜⁺'.
'Alors les projecteurs spectraux de x sont dans a': the variable is A (the operator of the crossed Proposition 1), not x. It probably reads 'les projecteurs spectraux de A … sont dans 𝔞'.
'A à une fonction φ sur C₀(Ω)': the manuscript slip is as transcribed, but the meaning is a function on Ω.

The whole block from 'Proposition 1 Soit A un opérateur normal dans b' to 'Corollaire Soit K(Ω) ⊂ a' is struck through with large diagonal strokes. The page's content was abandoned and rewritten as Proposition 5 on the next page.

The first two lines are mostly struck; the opening words are probably '[Voici …]' and 'Il …', and the surviving parenthesis likely explains 𝔟 as the closure of 𝔞 ('i.e. … adhérence de 𝔞'?) [uncertain].
